key_insight: Automated SkillOpt prompts greatly improved false-presupposition correction in cancer-question answering, but the gains varied by model and could increase over-correction.
clinical_relevance: For clinical NLP tools, prompt strategies should be tested on each target model using both false-presupposition correction and normal-question accuracy, not just one metric.
method: Compared SkillOpt-generated instructions with conventional prompting across seven LLMs
Used a physician-verified Cancer-Myth benchmark with FP and NFP questions
Evaluated rewritten skills on held-out questions with an external GPT-4o judge
evidence_signal: In GPT-4o, SkillOpt raised FP correction from about 15.4-17.6% to 82.2-90.5%, and compact versions improved NFP accuracy on some stronger models.
watch_item: SkillOpt was not universally portable and sometimes challenged valid clinical assumptions, so it needs model-specific validation before use.
paper_title: Automated Skill Optimisation for False Presupposition Handling in Cancer Communication: SkillOpt Versus Conventional Prompt Engineering Across Language Models
